Appendix B • Velocity Units Examples [3.2.3]

B.1 Redshift Independent Line Separation

The difference in wavelength between lines is redshift dependent, since, for a rest-frame: \begin{align} \Delta^{\alpha X}_\mathrm{rest} = \lambda_\alpha - \lambda_X. \tag{B.5} \end{align} However, our observer notices that the wavelength difference is given by: \begin{align} \Delta^{\alpha X}_\mathrm{obs} = \lambda^\alpha_\mathrm{obs}(\vec{x}) - \lambda^X_\mathrm{obs}(\vec{x}) = \left( \lambda_\alpha - \lambda_X \right) \frac{a_\mathrm{obs}}{a(\vec{x})} \tag{B.6} \end{align} This depends on the comoving position at which these lines were created.
However, using velocity units, if we fix the value of the anchor wavelength, \(\lambda_\dagger\), and of the reference scale factor, \(a_\dagger\), the observed difference would be given by: \begin{align} \Delta v^{\alpha X}_\mathrm{obs} = v_\dagger^\alpha\left(\vec{x}\right) - v_\dagger^X\left(\vec{x}\right) = c \ln\left( \frac{\lambda_\alpha}{\lambda_\dagger} \frac{a_\dagger}{a(\vec{x})} \right) - c \ln\left( \frac{\lambda_X}{\lambda_\dagger} \frac{a_\dagger}{a(\vec{x})} \right) = c\ln\left(\frac{\lambda_\alpha}{\lambda_X}\right) = \Delta v^{\alpha X}_\mathrm{rest} \tag{B.7} \end{align} This, as promised, is redshift independent.
